name: IEC C13/C14 (kettle AC inlet)
gender: C14 inlet (equipment, male pins) / C13 connector (cable, female)
ascii:
____________________
    |       ( E )        |    C14 AC inlet (equipment side)
    |                    |      E = earth / ground (top, longest)
    |  ( L )      ( N )  |      L = line (live)
    |____________________|      N = neutral
   ~120 / 230 V AC MAINS -- LETHAL. Earth mates first, breaks last.
description: The 3-pin AC mains connector on PCs, monitors, amps, and countless appliances (the 'kettle lead'). The C14 is the inlet on the equipment (male pins); the C13 is the socket on the cable (female). Three conductors: line (live), neutral, and protective earth. The earth pin is longer so it connects first and disconnects last.

contacts.name: EARTH
contacts.description: protective earth / ground (top pin, longest -- mates first, breaks last). Ties the chassis to ground

contacts.name: LINE
contacts.description: line / live (~120 V or ~230 V AC). LETHAL

contacts.name: NEUTRAL
contacts.description: neutral (near ground potential, but treat as live -- it can float)

variants: C13/C14 is the 10 A cold-condition type. The physically similar C15/C16 (a notch keys it) is the HOT type, rated to 120 C, used on kettles and some lab gear -- a C13 will not seat in a C16 inlet. The C19/C20 is the bigger 16 A type for servers/PSUs.
Regional cords: the C13 end is universal, but the wall plug on the other end (Schuko, NEMA 5-15, BS1363, etc.) is region-specific.
gotchas: This is MAINS voltage -- 120 V or 230 V AC, enough to kill. Never probe a live inlet; unplug and verify dead before touching pins.

The earth pin is longer by design: it must make contact before L/N on insertion and break after them on removal, so the chassis is grounded whenever the mains pins are live. Never defeat the earth pin.
Neutral is near ground but NOT safe -- a wiring fault or a reversed wall socket can leave neutral live. Treat both L and N as dangerous.
C13/C14 (cold) vs C15/C16 (hot, keyed notch): don't force a plain kettle lead into a hot-rated C16 inlet or vice-versa; the key exists for a reason.
notes: IEC 60320 C13/C14 3-pin mains (Earth/Line/Neutral). Earth = long pin, mates first. C15/C16 hot variant + C19/C20 16A variant noted. MAINS -- lethal.
